title: Erdős #848 OQ-01: Why Exactly {7, 18} mod 25?
description: Algebraic explanation for why {n ≡ 7 (mod 25)} and {n ≡ 18 (mod 25)} are the extremal sets: 7 and 18 are the unique solutions to x² ≡ -1 (mod 25). Proves the cross-residue incompatibility (5² ∤ ab+1 for a≡7, b≡18 mod 25), classifies all mod-25 residue classes, and gives an independent lower bound via the mod-18 witness.

meta.author: Erdős, Sárközy (1992); algebraic analysis
meta.assumptions: None. Fully verified with 0 axioms and 0 sorries.

overview.historicalContext: Erdős and Sárközy (1992) posed the problem of finding the maximum set A ⊆ {1,...,N} with ab+1 non-squarefree for all a,b ∈ A. The answer involves the residues 7 and 18 modulo 25. This file gives the algebraic explanation: 7² = 49 ≡ -1 (mod 25) and 18² = 324 ≡ -1 (mod 25), making these the two square roots of -1 in ℤ/25ℤ. The connection is: for a ≡ b ≡ x (mod 25), ab+1 ≡ x²+1 (mod 25). This is 0 (mod 25) exactly when x² ≡ -1 (mod 25), i.e., when x ∈ {7, 18}. No other residue class mod 25 works. Furthermore, the two classes cannot be combined: for a ≡ 7 and b ≡ 18 (mod 25), ab+1 ≡ 127 ≡ 2 (mod 25), so 5 ∤ ab+1.
overview.problemStatement: Why are {n ≡ 7 (mod 25)} and {n ≡ 18 (mod 25)} the extremal sets for Erdős #848? Specifically: (1) what algebraic property do 7 and 18 satisfy mod 25? (2) are these the only mod-25 classes with this property? (3) can the two classes be combined?
overview.text: 7 and 18 are the unique solutions to x² ≡ -1 (mod 25). This makes them the only mod-25 residue classes where a same-class pair (a,b) has 5² | ab+1 for all pairs. The two classes are incompatible: mixing them breaks the 5² condition on cross-pairs.
overview.proofStrategy: Part I uses decide for the ZMod 25 characterization. Part II uses ring algebra: for a = 25m+7 and b = 25n+18, ab+1 = 25*(25mn+18m+7n+5)+2, so 25 ∤ ab+1. Part III uses interval_cases to check all 25 residues. Part IV copies the mod-7 lower bound proof with offset 18 instead of 7.
keyInsights: 7² = 49 = 2·25 - 1 ≡ -1 (mod 25): the algebraic key connecting 7 to the property
18 = -7 in ℤ/25ℤ (since 7+18=25), so the two classes are ±√(-1) mod 25
Classification is complete: interval_cases checks all 25 residues and only r=7,18 work
The lower bound proof for mod-18 is structurally identical to mod-7 (offset 18 vs 7)
prerequisites: ZMod 25 arithmetic and decide tactic for finite enumeration
Modular arithmetic: a ≡ b (mod 25) → a² ≡ b² (mod 25)
Quadratic residues: x² ≡ -1 (mod p) has solutions iff p ≡ 1 (mod 4)

sections.title: Part I: Algebraic Explanation via ZMod 25
sections.summary: Proves seven_sq_eq_neg_one_mod25, eighteen_sq_eq_neg_one_mod25, seven_eq_neg_eighteen_mod25, sq_neg_one_iff_seven_or_eighteen (uniqueness), and mod25_sq_succ_dvd_iff (elementary ℕ form).
sections.mathContext: 7² ≡ -1 (mod 25) and 18² ≡ -1 (mod 25), and these are the only solutions. 18 = -7 in ℤ/25ℤ.

sections.title: Part II: Cross-Residue Incompatibility
sections.summary: Proves cross_residue_five_sq_fails (a≡7, b≡18 → 5²∤ab+1), its symmetric version, and mixed_set_needs_other_prime (a mixed set must rely on other primes for cross pairs).
sections.mathContext: For a = 25m+7, b = 25n+18: ab+1 = 25*(25mn+18m+7n+5)+2. The remainder 2 shows 25 ∤ ab+1.

sections.title: Part III: Complete Classification of Mod-25 Classes
sections.summary: Proves non_extremal_class_five_sq_fails (all r ∉ {7,18} with r < 25 fail) and extremal_iff_five_sq_divides (complete biconditional characterization).
sections.mathContext: For r < 25: 5² | r·r+1 iff r = 7 or r = 18. Proved by interval_cases checking all 25 residues.

sections.title: Part IV: Independent Mod-18 Lower Bound
sections.summary: Constructs mod18Set, proves it has the non-squarefree product property and cardinality ≥ N/25. Concludes lower_bound_via_mod18: N/25 ≤ maxNonSqfreeSet N for N ≥ 25.
sections.mathContext: The injection k ↦ 25k+18 maps {0,...,N/25-1} into {n ≤ N : n ≡ 18 (mod 25)}, giving the lower bound.

conclusion.summary: The algebraic explanation for Erdős #848's extremal structure is fully formalized: 7 and 18 are the unique square roots of -1 in ℤ/25ℤ (proved by decide), all other mod-25 residue classes fail (proved by interval_cases), the two classes are incompatible for cross-pairs (proved by ring+omega), and an independent lower bound N/25 ≤ maxNonSqfreeSet N is given via the mod-18 witness. 0 sorries, 0 axioms.
conclusion.implications: The connection between Erdős #848 and ZMod 25 square roots of -1 is now fully formalized. This algebraic perspective explains why the problem is governed by modular arithmetic: the extremal configuration is determined by the quadratic residue structure of ℤ/25ℤ, specifically the solutions to x² ≡ -1 (mod 25). The incompatibility result shows why the two classes are rigid: any set mixing both residue types must rely on other prime squares for cross-pairs, making it harder to maintain the non-squarefree product property globally.
openQuestions: Can the cross-residue incompatibility be strengthened: for a≡7, b≡18 (mod 25), is ab+1 always squarefree? (For a=7, b=18: 7·18+1=127 is prime, so squarefree. But in general, ab+1 might have large prime square factors.)
Can Hensel's lemma be used to lift the mod-25 analysis to mod-625 (5⁴), giving a tighter bound than N/25?
The van Doorn upper bound (≤ 0.108N from the parent file) involves an infinite sum over primes p ≡ 1 (mod 4). Can this sum be formally evaluated in Lean 4?
